articles.headline: Four men arrested in connection with Feb. shooting of 49ers' Keion White
articles.description: Four men have been arrested in connection with the shooting of 49ers defensive lineman Keion White at a nightclub in February, officials said Wednesday.
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO -- Four men have been arrested in connection with the shooting of 49ers defensive lineman Keion White at a nightclub in February, officials said Wednesday.

The shooting occurred just after 4 a.m. on Feb. 9 at the crowded Mission District nightclub Dahlia, where White was hosting a private Super Bowl party.

White was shot in the ankle and taken to a local hospital for surgery, the 49ers said at the time.

San Francisco Police Chief Derrick Lew said authorities arrested four men over the past week with the help of law enforcement agencies in Atlanta; Stockton, California; Irvine, California and Los Angeles.

The night of the shooting, multiple suspects with firearms "confronted" White, Lew said. Investigators used video footage and witness accounts to identify the men they say are the perpetrators.

On Oct. 7, local law enforcement arrested 35-year-old Curtis Green in Irvine, and two days later authorities arrested 36-year-old Gregory Walker of Mountain House, California, for their alleged involvement in the shooting.

The men were booked into San Francisco County Jail on Monday and scheduled to appear in court Wednesday afternoon. District Attorney Brooke Jenkins said prosecutors would seek no bail for Walker because of the public safety risk they said he poses. He will be charged with assault with a semiautomatic firearm -- which prosecutors say he fired -- as well as other charges for having a gun as a felon.

Green faces misdemeanor charges of brandishing a firearm and carrying a concealed and loaded gun in public, Jenkins said.

A message was left Wednesday with the San Francisco public defender's office to determine if its attorneys were representing the two men.

Two other men arrested in other jurisdictions are not yet in local custody and will be charged once they are brought to San Francisco, Jenkins said.

One of the other men expected to face charges in San Francisco was arrested Oct. 7 in Atlanta. The 38-year-old was arrested on a no-bail warrant. Authorities say police seized an illegal firearm during the arrest, along with thousands of grams of MDMA, methamphetamine, cocaine and fentanyl at the man's home.

That same day, law enforcement arrested a 36-year-old man in Stockton, California, in connection with White's shooting, and recovered a loaded firearm, over 100 oxycodone pills and $7,000 in cash.

White has appeared in all five games this season for the 49ers, totaling three sacks. 

Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

articles.headline: Rams' Alaric Jackson has suspension cut to 1 game following appeal
articles.description: Alaric Jackson's suspension for punching Bradley Chubb after Monday night's game between the Bills and Rams was reduced from two games to one.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- Alaric Jackson's suspension for punching Bradley Chubb after Monday night's game between the Buffalo Bills and Los Angeles Rams was reduced from two games to one, the NFL said Wednesday.

The Rams' left tackle had appealed Tuesday's ruling by the league. Hearing officer Derrick Brooks, who was jointly appointed by the NFL and the NFL Players Association, heard the appeal and reduced the punishment to one game.

The league initially said Jackson violated Rule 12, Section 3, Article 1, which applies to "any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship," when he struck Chubb following the Rams' 37-34 overtime loss in Los Angeles on Monday. 

"Have to make better decisions than that," Rams coach Sean McVay said Tuesday.

Jackson now will sit out only the Rams' Week 6 game against the Arizona Cardinals. David Quessenberry will start in his place, McVay said Tuesday.

In a scene captured by ESPN's cameras, Jackson stood near midfield following Monday's game while exchanging jerseys with Bills defensive lineman Deone Walker when Chubb said something to him. Jackson then walked toward Chubb before punching the linebacker in the face with his right hand.

On Wednesday, Chubb told reporters that he initiated the conversation with Jackson.

"I've heard I was talking about his mom," Chubb said. "That's not true at all. I said: 'We're gonna see y'all's ass again. And when we see you again, all that chipping ain't gonna save you. That tight end and guard is not going to save you.' He said, 'What'd you say?' I said, 'That chip's not gonna save you. The guard's not gonna save you.' And then boom."

Chubb said he hasn't heard from Jackson since the incident.

"We're going to learn from it," Chubb said. "Me personally, I learned I'm either going to have my hands up or wear a helmet."

This is Jackson's second NFL suspension. He sat out for two games in 2024 for violating the NFL's personal conduct policy.

ESPN's Nick Suss contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Bills' Bradley Chubb details his side of altercation with Rams' Alaric Jackson
articles.description: Bills edge defender Bradley Chubb gave his side of the story two days after a postgame altercation with Rams offensive tackle Alaric Jackson.
articles.body:
IRVINE, Calif. -- Buffalo Bills veteran edge defender Bradley Chubb shared his side of the story two days after taking a punch from Los Angeles Rams offensive tackle Alaric Jackson in the moments following the Bills' overtime win on "Monday Night Football."

"I'll tell you exactly what I said," Chubb told reporters Wednesday at the practice facility on UC Irvine's campus, where the Bills are practicing this week ahead of Sunday's game against the Las Vegas Raiders. "I've heard I was talking about his mom. That's not true at all. I said, 'We're gonna see y'all's ass again. And when we see you again, all that chipping ain't gonna save you. That tight end and guard is not going to save you.' He said, 'What'd you say?' I said, 'That chip's not gonna save you. The guard's not gonna save you.' And then boom."

Chubb acknowledged that he initiated the conversation. As video of the incident shows, Jackson was in the middle of a jersey swap with Bills defensive tackle Deone Walker when Chubb caught his attention.

Chubb said one of the things that caught his ire was a perception that the Rams were "front-running." Put another way, Chubb said he felt the Rams' trash talk started to intensify only when they thought they were going to win the game. After Bills defender Greg Rousseau blocked the Rams' overtime field goal attempt to tip the game's odds back toward the Bills, the tenor changed.

Jackson was initially suspended two games by the NFL for the punch, but that was reduced to one game Wednesday after he appealed.

Chubb said he was proud that he didn't respond with his own punch, saying the Bills signed him to play and to be a good leader, and that getting into a fight wouldn't have been a good example of either. But he conceded culpability in the incident, and said he and his teammates have plenty to learn.

The Rams and Bills aren't scheduled to play again in 2026. For the teams to face off again, it will have to be in the Super Bowl, which Chubb sees as a distinct possibility.

Chubb said he hasn't heard from Jackson since the incident.

"We're going to learn from it," Chubb said. "Me personally, I learned I'm either going to have my hands up or wear a helmet."

articles.headline: Seahawks rule out LB Thomas, RB Charbonnet for Thursday night game vs. Broncos
articles.description: The Seahawks will be without starting linebacker Drake Thomas and running back Zach Charbonnet for Thursday's game at Denver.
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks ruled out starting linebacker Drake Thomas and running back Zach Charbonnet for their Thursday night game against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High.

Wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba and defensive tackle Leonard Williams have no game designations. They are both dealing with ankle injuries that had them listed as limited on the Seahawks' first two practice reports of the week, which were estimations because the team did not practice Monday or Tuesday.

Williams was again listed as limited Wednesday, and Smith-Njigba was listed as a full participant.

"Those guys, they're ready to play," coach Mike Macdonald said of Smith-Njigba and Williams. "Looked good. On the short week, it's unfortunate we lost a couple of guys. Drake got out of the game and other guys are still out, but we're in a good spot."

Thomas injured an ankle in the Seahawks' loss to the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday. He returned to the game and finished it but has been listed as a non-participant during all three days this week.

Macdonald confirmed that Tyrice Knight will start at weakside linebacker in Thomas' absence. A 2024 fourth-round pick, Knight made nine starts as a rookie and four last year.

"We're confident he'll play great and the standard stays the same on defense," Macdonald said. "I know he's excited for the opportunity and we're excited to see him play."

Charbonnet, a co-starter last season, is still working his way back from February ACL surgery. Macdonald said postgame Sunday that the team was not planning to play him against Denver, though he didn't rule it out.

Charbonnet has been listed as limited on every injury report since the Seahawks designated him to return to practice on Oct. 1. They have until Oct. 22 to activate him off the physically unable to perform list.

"He looks tremendous," Macdonald said. "Working through it on how we're going to handle the situation. Right now, our focus is on playing a game. He's not playing in this game. He's going to be cheering us on and then we'll move forward. We're not even at nine months. ... It's remarkable that we're having this conversation."

With Charbonnet still on PUP and rookie first-round pick Jadarian Price (chest) on injured reserve for at least two more games, Emanuel Wilson and George Holani will continue to lead Seattle's backfield. Velus Jones Jr. is the team's third running back.

The only other Seahawk with an injury designation is backup linebacker/special teamer Chazz Surratt, who's out with an ankle injury.

The Broncos will be without All-Pro cornerback Patrick Surtain II and safety Talanoa Hufanga, who both have ankle injuries. Cornerback Riley Moss, who starts opposite Surtain, is questionable due to a rib injury.

articles.headline: Mourinho takes blame for Madrid struggles before late rally stuns Roma
articles.description: José Mourinho took the blame for Real Madrid's struggles at Roma in the Champions League on Wednesday, praising his players for leading a seven-minute comeback to turn a 3-1 deficit into a 4-3 win.
articles.body:
ROME -- José Mourinho took the blame for Real Madrid's struggles at AS Roma in the Champions League on Wednesday, before praising his players for leading a seven-minute comeback to turn a 3-1 deficit into a 4-3 win.

Substitutes Carlos Espí and Endrick each scored before a 90th-minute header from Antonio Rüdiger -- with Arda Güler providing his second assist of the night -- gave Madrid maximum points in the league phase so far.

- Kirkland: A seven-minute stretch saved a weak Real Madrid team from a humbling Champions League crash

- Madrid's Vini Jr. gets 4-game ban after hair-pull red card; will miss Clásico

In his postmatch news conference, Mourinho said he'd been outsmarted by counterpart Gian Piero Gasperini, before making the necessary tactical changes after the break.

"The first half was the coach's fault; the second half was the players' fault," Mourinho said. "Football is a 90-minute, strategic game. Opponents matter, and today's opponent was incredibly strong. They are a formidable team.

"But it's impossible to play at that intensity, the way they played, for a full 90 minutes. I made the substitutions I thought were necessary. But in the first half, they really punished us."

Mourinho introduced Endrick -- for Vinícius Júnior -- and Güler in the 59th minute, before adding Espí and Bernardo Silva as Madrid searched desperately for a way back into the game.

Vinícius told reporters afterward that he hadn't understood the switch, saying it was "natural to be angry" while acknowledging that the change had paid off.

"It was tough for Vini," Mourinho said. "Vini lost a ball he shouldn't have lost [for Roma's second goal]. But that's how it goes. I make mistakes, too. It's a shame that this happened, just as he was growing and finding happiness again.

"It's natural for him not to be happy. ... Frustration is normal. But after the match, he was very happy about the win."

Mourinho was treated like a returning hero at Stadio Olimpico on Wednesday at the home of one of his former clubs.

Before kickoff, there was a long applause when the stadium announcer read out the teams and Mourinho's name. Then, early in the first half, at the end of the stadium where Roma's hard-core "ultra" fans sit, they held up three huge signs featuring images of Mourinho -- one of which depicted him cradling the Conference League trophy that Roma won in 2022 to conclude his first season in charge.

The Conference League title was Roma's first significant European trophy.

Mourinho also led Roma to the Europa League final in 2023. He left the club in January 2024 without really saying goodbye.

"Whoever brings glory to Rome, Rome will honor forever," read one of the banners. "The people bestow you with eternal glory."

Mourinho said he was left "speechless" by the reception.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Warriors' Kristaps Porzingis remains out indefinitely but will be around team
articles.description: Warriors center Kristaps Porzingis will remain out indefinitely with a private health-related issue but will be around the team.
articles.headlineJa: ウォリアーズのクリスタプス・ポルジンギス、引き続き無期限欠場となるがチームには帯同
articles.descriptionJa: ウォリアーズのセンター、クリスタプス・ポルジンギスは、プライベートな健康上の問題により引き続き無期限で欠場するが、チームには帯同する予定だ。
articles.body:
Kristaps Porzingis will remain out indefinitely with a private health-related issue, the Golden State Warriors announced Wednesday, but the veteran center will remain around the team.

"I'm working with doctors and experts to figure out how to be fully back to good health (as soon as possible)," Porzingis said on social media. "Honestly, I'm getting better and better. I just have to stay patient, and I believe I'll be feeling great again soon."

Porzingis called general manager Mike Dunleavy on the eve of training camp and informed the organization that he wouldn't be reporting. He didn't attend the team's trip to Hawaii and missed the first five preseason games.

While his coaches and teammates were in Las Vegas for a preseason game against the Los Angeles Lakers on Tuesday night, Porzingis returned to the Warriors' downtown San Francisco facility and met with Dunleavy and lead medical decision-maker Rick Celebrini.

In a statement, the Warriors said they'd keep the details of that meeting private, but Porzingis is expected to be in the facility and around the team as they wrap up preseason and prepare for the regular season opener next Wednesday in Los Angeles against the Lakers.

"It has definitely been frustrating dealing with some health stuff that you can't exactly pinpoint, on top of injuries throughout my career," Porzingis wrote in an X post. "So it has added up for sure, but we will get through it."

Porzingis is not yet cleared to practice and the team said it would update his "potential resumption of practice, playing status and timeline" whenever available and appropriate.

Two seasons ago, Porzingis contracted an upper respiratory virus while playing for the Boston Celtics, and he has since vaguely revealed the lingering impact it has had on his health and ability to consistently play NBA basketball.

Porzingis was limited to 34 games last season, split between the Atlanta Hawks and Warriors, who traded Jonathan Kuminga for him in February. Golden State then re-signed Porzingis to a two-year, $40 million deal this summer.

The contract was structured strategically to allow the Warriors to trade Porzingis at any point and limit their long-term downside. Only $3 million of the $20 million next season is guaranteed.

In his absence, coach Steve Kerr said he is leaning toward starting a smaller lineup of Stephen Curry, Brandin Podziemski, Gui Santos, Yaxel Lendeborg and Draymond Green.

articles.headline: Marvin Harrison Jr. will play for Texans on Sunday in London, coach says
articles.description: Texans wideout Marvin Harrison Jr. will play against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London on Sunday, Houston coach DeMeco Ryans said Wednesday.
articles.headlineJa: マービン・ハリソン・ジュニア、日曜にロンドンでテキサンズの一員として出場へ。コーチが発表
articles.descriptionJa: ヒューストンのデメコ・ライアンズコーチは水曜日、テキサンズのワイドレシーバー、マービン・ハリソン・ジュニアが日曜日にロンドンで行われるジャクソンビル・ジャガーズ戦に出場することを明らかにした。
articles.body:
HOUSTON -- Newly acquired Texans wideout Marvin Harrison Jr. will play against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London on Sunday, Houston coach DeMeco Ryans said Wednesday.

It's a quick turnaround for Harrison, as he just arrived in Houston on Monday. The Texans (1-4) sent 2027 second- and seventh-round picks to the Arizona Cardinals to acquire Harrison and a 2027 sixth-round selection after a disappointing start to his career with the Cards.

Harrison has just five catches on 13 targets for 85 yards and a touchdown this season. But he said Wednesday he views the new chapter as a "great" opportunity as he reunites with his college quarterback C.J. Stroud. They played together in 2021 and 2022 at Ohio State, and both were All-Americans.

"I think the team as a whole it's a great situation for me," Harrison said of the Texans. "Being with a quarterback that you have rapport with and had success with in the past is always great too."

The No. 4 pick in the 2024 NFL draft joins Houston with an underwhelming career stat line of 1,578 yards, 13 touchdowns and 108 receptions in 33 games. When asked why he didn't produce in Arizona, he said he is "going to take accountability" but that he wants to keep specific information confidential.

"I think it's just a combination of everything," Harrison said. "I don't think I can pinpoint one thing. There's a lot of factors, and I think with any situation, you always want to take accountability for yourself.

"I think those things I'll keep to myself, truthfully. What I learned in Arizona, I definitely learned a lot. But like I said, I'm really just looking forward."

Harrison passed the physical on Monday and practiced with Houston for the first time Wednesday. There will be an acclimation process for him where he'll learn the playbook, but Ryans said he isn't worried about the learning part, citing Harrison's work ethic.

"It isn't hard when the player is attentive and he's locked in on getting the details down," Ryans said. "Marvin's first night here, he was with our assistant wide receiver coach Tiquan [Underwood] and they were grinding. They were working late at night. They were in the playbook grinding, and that allowed him to get a day ahead. And now, he was able to go out there today and just fit right in seamlessly."

Stroud said he was happy Houston included him in the discussion regarding acquiring the wide receiver. But now that Harrison is a Texan, the team will have to fit him into the offense.

Harrison is joining a wideout room led by Nico Collins, Xavier Hutchinson and Jaylin Noel. Stroud is humming through five weeks, ranking fifth in passing yards with 1,402.

The former college duo will lean on old experiences to rekindle chemistry, Stroud said, which is why he doesn't think the adjustment will take long.

"He's a really smart kid. I'm not worried about it," Stroud said of Harrison. "At the end of day, it's football. You run some very similar routes, just different ways, and I'm very vocal on how

articles.headline: Andoni Iraola: Bradley Barcola hat trick will help him settle in at Liverpool
articles.description: Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola said he hopes Bradley Barcola's first Champions League hat trick will provide the confidence boost the winger needs to settle into life at his new club.
articles.body:
Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola said he hopes Bradley Barcola's first Champions League hat trick will provide the confidence boost the winger needs to settle into life at his new club.

The £123 million ($163m) summer signing is no stranger to success at Europe's elite level, having won the competition the last two seasons with Paris Saint-Germain, but in his first six appearances he was the shadow of the player the Reds thought they were buying.

But against Champions League debutants LASK, Barcola sparked into life, scoring a goal with either foot before adding a simple tap in for his third in the 6-3 rout of their Austrian hosts.

"I'm really happy for Bradley because you were asking me yesterday about him not making the numbers, also Florian [Wirtz]," said Iraola.

"I think both of them today played really well. I think they made a difference. Bradley apart from the hat trick, I think he was a threat always -- one-v-one, threatening in behind.

"Also Flo helped us a lot to control the game, finding the pockets. I'm happy for both of them.

"I think their confidence, for sure, is very good. I think they feel that we trust them a lot. But at the end, to enjoy a little bit playing in the Champions League away, I think it's going to be very good for them."

On the difference it will make to Barcola, Iraola added: "Obviously I think he has to enjoy this because to score a hat trick in the Champions League is always very difficult.

"Even training yesterday, I could feel he was very lively -- sometimes you feel these things. You never know how he's going to play the next day, but it wasn't like a big surprise because we were feeling he was in a good place for the game."

After Sunday's 3-0 defeat to Manchester City, their first loss of the season, this was the ideal response against sub-standard opposition and the fact Iraola was able to rest the likes of Virgil van Dijk and Alexis Mac Allister ahead of the weekend trip to Brentford was also helpful.

Lewis Koumas scored his first in the Champions League, with goals also from Ronald Araújo -- his maiden strike for the club -- and Jeremie Frimpong, while 19-year-old midfielder Trey Nyoni played 85 minutes on his second start of the season.

- Barcola nets hat trick for 1st Liverpool goals in 6-goal UCL rout of LASK Linz

- Alisson misses Mohamed Salah but Liverpool 'move on'

- Transfer rumors, news: Liverpool eye move for Juventus' Kalulu

"You have different demands for each game and you have to try to analyse what players, not just you can rest, it's what players can perform well against LASK and help us to win the game, what players can help us against Brentford," added Iraola.

"But after Brentford we will play in three days against Villarreal, another very difficult Champions League game, and we will need more than 11, more than 12, more than 13.

"That's why I'm very happy because especially the young players with less experience can give us good performances and also add some experience.

articles.headline: Halftime lead worried Luis Enrique in game PSG 'could have lost' to City
articles.description: Luis Enrique said PSG only want to be best team "at the end of the season" after the back-to-back Champions League winners sealed a 4-2 win at Manchester City.
articles.body:
MANCHESTER, England -- Luis Enrique said Paris Saint-Germain "could have lost" their Champions League match Manchester City after racing out to a 3-0 lead at halftime at the Etihad on Wednesday.

PSG went on to win 4-2 after a dominant first half -- and hit the post and missed a penalty in a second half -- as City fought back after the break through two goals from Erling Haaland.

Although his side ended up comfortable winners, the PSG coach said his team's early lead didn't help PSG.

"How proud am I? It's hard to say because the match had very different moments," Luis Enrique said. "In the first half, we showed what we want to do as a team, but I don't like going into halftime with a 3-0 lead.

"Most think the game is won, but it's never the case and even with less luck, we can lose this kind of game. We suffered a lot in the second half, they deserved to score more goals. With a bit of bad luck, we could have lost this match"

The former Barcelona coach added that PSG only want to be the best team "at the end of the season" as the back-to-back Champions League winners look ahead a clash with his former team that will feature the top clubs in the League Phase table so far.

The French champions face second-placed Barcelona at Parc des Princes next Tuesday, but despite beating City and having the chance to beat the Spanish champions, the PSG coach said the most important factor is being the best in May, not October.

"PSG vs. Barça next? Being the best team at this stage of the season is not the most important thing," Luis Enrique said. "The most important thing is to be the best team at the end of the season."

PSG are aiming to emulate Real Madrid by winning a third successive Champions League this season.

Luis Enrique's opposite number for PSG's next Champions League test, Hansi Flick, said nearly the same after Barcelona rolled to a 4-1 win over Galatasaray on Tuesday to extend his team's perfect start to the season to 10 games across competitions.

"Football can change very fast," Flick said Tuesday when asked if Barça are unstoppable. "We are proud about this situation. We are happy and we have not just the confidence, but also the conviction in our style, how we want to play.

"But our ambitions are more; we want to win titles. We can win nothing now. In May, June you win the big titles. We are working every day for that."

articles.headline: Real Madrid's Vinícius Junior gets 4-game ban after red card; will miss Clásico
articles.description: Vinícius Junior has been handed a four-game ban for his sending-off in Real Madrid's LaLiga win over Villarreal and will miss this month's Clásico with Barcelona.
articles.body:
Vinícius Junior has been handed a four-game ban for his sending-off in Real Madrid's LaLiga win over Villarreal and will miss this month's Clásico with Barcelona.

The Spanish football federation's disciplinary committee confirmed on Wednesday that the Madrid forward had been given a two-game ban for violent conduct after pulling Nathan Saliba's hair during Saturday's match at the Bernabéu, and another two games for his angry reaction to the decision.

Moments after the hair pull, Vinícius converted Jude Bellingham's pass to put Madrid 2-0 up, before a VAR review of the incident saw the goal disallowed, and the Brazil international shown a red card.

Coach José Mourinho left Vinícius out of Madrid's starting XI against Villarreal after a difficult start to the season, in which he has scored just once for his club.

Vinícius, who apologized to fans on social media afterward, will now miss Madrid's game with Sevilla on Sunday, the Clásico at Camp Nou on Sunday, Oct. 25, and matches against Racing Santander and Valencia.

Following Real Madrid's dramatic 4-3 Champions League comeback victory over Roma on Wednesday, Vinícius questioned the timing of his domestic suspension and insisted he has never been violent toward another player.

"They had all day to announce the suspension, yet just as we arrived at the stadium, I was told I'm out for four league games," the Brazilian star said.

"We've never had this [hair pulling] explained to us. Someone from La Liga and the referees' association always comes to explain the rules, but never this specific point. It was a red card for me, simple as that... I've never been violent towards another player. I get hit quite a lot, yet the cards end up going to me." 

The ban is only applicable in domestic competitions, so Mourinho named Vinícius in the starting XI for Wednesday's Champions League game at Roma. He will also be available for games with RB Leipzig on Oct. 21 and AEK on Nov. 4.

"The question for the committee is why they released the punishment in this moment," Mourinho told Movistar. "If you ask that question, it's because you think it could affect him. If not, you wouldn't ask me the question.

"I think you should ask the committee why they didn't do it this morning, or tomorrow morning, and why they do it two hours before an important game for Real Madrid, without forgetting that Real Madrid are a Spanish club."

Vinícius will next play a LaLiga match after November's international break.

The committee said Vinícius had received a two-game ban for "violent conduct, without the possibility of playing the ball" and the two additional games for arguing with the referee "with an aggressive attitude and having to be restrained by his teammates."

Vinícius signed a new long-term contract at Madrid until 2032 this summer, after being heavily linked with a move away having entered the last year of his previous deal.

articles.description: The NBA regular season is less than a week away, and we're tracking all the news, deals, and trades across the league.
articles.headlineJa: NBAプレシーズン最新情報：トレード、ニュース、内部情報をチェック
articles.descriptionJa: NBAレギュラーシーズン開幕まで1週間を切り、リーグ全体のあらゆるニュース、契約、トレードの動向を追っています。
articles.body:
With the preseason games coming to a close soon, the 2026-27 NBA season is less than a week away from tipping off.

How will LeBron James and Jaylen Brown look on the court in their new Philadelphia 76ers uniforms? What will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first season away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their impact this season?

Check back here for all the latest buzz, news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders, with the latest info at the top:

Quick links:

Free agency grades | Trade grades

Trade tracker | Transactions | Offseason buzz

Depth charts | Trade machine | More

Oct. 14

Hoop Collective: The biggest questions in the NBA's Central Division

Brian is joined by ESPN's Vincent Goodwill and Tim MacMahon to preview the NBA's Central Division, including the biggest questions facing the five teams. Is this another make-or-break season for the Cleveland Cavaliers? Will the Detroit Pistons repeat their 2025-26 success? And, can Tyrese Haliburton's return vault the Indiana Pacers back up the Eastern Conference standings? They tackle all this and more in the latest episode of the Hoop Collective podcast.

Topics:

0:15: Our 2026-27 Central Division preview

4:25: Lots of big questions for the Pistons

11:43: Make or break season for the Cavaliers

27:50: Can Haliburton bring back the Pacers?

35:30: Bucks post-Giannis future looks murky

42:05: Young talent is intriguing with the Bulls

Windhorst on if the Cavaliers can improve their roster: "Jarrett Allen is the guy that they would have to do something with. And the thing about it is that they can't trade Jarrett Allen because you'd need a franchise center. And that means Evan Mobley would probably have to be your franchise center.

"First off, if you're trading Jarrett Allen, are you upgrading at center for trading Jarrett Allen? No, you're probably upgrading somewhere else and you're asking Evan Mobley to play center. And Evan Mobley has not proven, even though a lot of people believe that he would be at his best playing full-time stretch center, [he can do that]. That's not something they've been able to get Evan to do consistently well. But that's the move that they have. The move that they have if they have to do something is to look at Jarrett Allen.

"But we'll see how that plays out. The Cavs are in a tough spot in that they are going to be expected to improve on last season, which the pathway to improve on a conference final season, it's a narrow path. And they're doing it in a much more competitive Eastern Conference landscape."

Pritchard agrees to two-year extension in Boston

Boston Celtics' guard Payton Pritchard has agreed a to a two-year, $44.2 million extension with the franchise, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Pritchard averaged career highs in points (17), assists (5.2) and rebounds (3.9) last season.

articles.body:
The ESPN fantasy basketball experts got together for their final points league mock draft before the start of the NBA season, which tips off Tuesday, Oct. 20.

So what changed since our earlier mock draft from three weeks ago?

Egor Demin and Matas Buzelis both were picked 30-plus spots higher, for one. Ryan Rollins, Darius Acuff Jr. and Jaden McDaniels were the other big risers compared to our Sept. 24 mock draft.

articles.headline: New era begins as Jayson Tatum and the Celtics embark on 1st season without Jaylen Brown
articles.description:
Boston Celtics 
              Last season: 58-26, lost to Philadelphia in first round of playoffs.
articles.body:
Boston Celtics 
              Last season: 58-26, lost to Philadelphia in first round of playoffs.


              COACH: Joe Mazzulla (5th season, 238-90).


              SEASON OPENER: Oct. 20 at Detroit.


              DEPARTURES: F Jaylen Brown, C Nikola Vucevic, F Anfernee Simons.


              ADDITIONS: F Paul George, C Mitchell Robinson, G Mike Conley Jr. 


              What to expect 
              It's a new era in Boston following the offseason trade of Brown to the Philadelphia 76ers. Only a few pieces remain from the core of the Celtics 2023-24 championship team. And there are lots of questions surrounding how this new version of the team will look without the homegrown tandem of Brown and Tatum that literally grew into the pillars of the franchise. Mazzulla has proven an ability to get the best out of what he has to work with, as evidenced in how the team played without Tatum last season as he recovered from rupturing his right Achilles tendon 17 months ago. But this may be the biggest test of Mazzulla's tenure as he looks to not only integrate new pieces, but make adjustments to an offense that has previously relied so heavily on 3-point shooting.


              Strengths and weaknesses


              The good: It starts with Tatum, who looks to be fully back to himself physically after rehabiliation from his surgery caused him to miss all but 16 regular season games and then Game 7 of their playoff loss to the 76ers because of a knee stiffness. George also enters the season healthy and at age 36 is poised to build off his strong playoff performance with the 76ers last season. Robinson’s presence brings an instant upgrade in rim protection, while also giving this group some great depth and options at center. Neemias Queta will likely remain the starter, but with plenty of support from both Robinson and Luka Garza. 


              The not-so-good: Brown’s departure breaks up the dynamic between he and Tatum that worked so well for nine seasons and eventually netted Boston its 18th NBA title. George says he’s more than willing to yield to Tatum, but that will put the weight on Tatum’s shoulders to carry the team, a burden he hasn’t had to bear alone yet during his career. 


              Players to watch
              Derrick White has tweaked the mechanics of his shot after a rough shooting year and will get more opportunities with Brown gone. Payton Pritchard started a career-high 50 games and average career bests in points (17.0), assists (5.2) and rebounds (3.9) last season coming off winning NBA Sixth Man of the Year honors in 2024-25. Last season also showed that he plays better coming off the bench, a role he’s expected to remain in barring injuries. Hugo Gonzalez also looks more skilled and comfortable at the NBA level as he prepares for Year 2.
